detailed_task_description: Open a receipt PDF from the desktop expenses folder, extract the expense details from the visible receipt, and then record that expense in a Google Sheets tracker. The workflow captures the merchant, purchased item description, item price, and total paid from the receipt as structured data. It then launches Google Chrome, opens the expenses spreadsheet, and enters a new expense row in the appropriate columns. The sheet entry should use the extracted receipt information for the expense description and cost while also filling any required structural fields such as the next sequential index.
success_criteria: Verify that the expenses Google Sheet contains a newly added row with the required structural fields completed and the expense description and cost accurately entered from the extracted receipt data.

subtasks.text: Open the expenses folder and receipt PDF so the receipt is visible for review. Expected outcome: The receipt PDF is open and visible on screen.

steps.expected_current_state: macOS desktop is visible with icons and widgets; a blue folder labeled "expenses" is present on the desktop and is not yet open in a Finder window.
steps.intent: Open the 'expenses' folder on the desktop to view its contents.

target.primary: Blue folder icon with the label "expenses" on the desktop (near the top-right area of the screen).

post_action: A Finder window opens for the folder, showing the folder's contents in a list.
The folder's files become visible in the newly opened window.

steps.expected_current_state: macOS desktop showing a Finder window for the 'expenses' folder with a list of files; a PDF file row labeled 'Receipt - SFO-A Black Point Cafe.pdf' is visible near the top of the list and selectable.
steps.intent: Open the PDF file so its receipt contents can be viewed in a PDF viewer.

target.primary: File row labeled 'Receipt - SFO-A Black Point Cafe.pdf' in the Finder file list (near the top-center of the Finder window)

post_action: A PDF viewer window opens displaying the document contents.
The Finder window remains in the background.

subtasks.text: Extract the merchant name, item line description, item price, and total paid from the visible receipt into extract_0. Expected outcome: The value for extract_0 is captured.

steps.expected_current_state: PDF viewer window showing a receipt document in the main/center panel (receipt header and body text visible). Left tools sidebar is open and the receipt text (merchant name, item lines, totals) is visible in the document pane.
steps.intent: Capture the bill details and final total from the visible receipt PDF. Example extracted content: sml cappucino at black point cafe, $7.16

target.primary: Receipt text in the main PDF viewer (center panel) under the 'Gmail' logo and the heading 'Receipt - SFO-A Black Point Cafe'.

post_action: not relevant

additional_args.extract_query: From the visible receipt area of the PDF, extract the merchant name, each purchased item description with its price (item lines), and the final total paid amount. Return structured fields: merchant_name, item_description, item_price, total_paid.

subtasks.text: Launch Google Chrome and open the Expenses Google Sheet from the bookmarks bar. Expected outcome: The expenses spreadsheet is open and ready for data entry.

steps.expected_current_state: macOS desktop with the Spotlight search overlay open near the top center of the screen; the Spotlight text field is focused and ready for input, with a PDF viewer window visible behind it.
steps.intent: Find and open the Google Chrome application by typing its name into Spotlight.

target.primary: Spotlight search text field near the top-center of the screen with placeholder text 'Spotlight Search'.

post_action: The Spotlight search field is populated with the typed text.
Search results appear below the field and a matching app result is highlighted.

steps.expected_current_state: macOS Spotlight search pop-up is open over the desktop with the query 'chrome' entered; a list of search results is visible with an item for Google Chrome near the top.
steps.intent: Select the 'Google Chrome' result from the Spotlight search results.

target.primary: Search result row showing the Google Chrome icon and the label 'Google Chrome' near the top of the Spotlight pop-up

post_action: The 'Google Chrome' search result is selected and highlighted.
Spotlight remains displayed showing the selected result.

steps.expected_current_state: Mac desktop with Spotlight search overlay open in the center showing results for 'chrome'; the list includes an app result labeled 'Google Chrome' and a search field at the top. Other apps/windows are visible in the background.
steps.intent: Open the Google Chrome application from the Spotlight results.

target.primary: Result row labeled 'Google Chrome' in the Spotlight search results (center overlay)

post_action: Google Chrome launches and becomes the frontmost application.
A Chrome browser window appears (showing a webpage) on screen.

steps.expected_current_state: A Chrome browser window with multiple tabs open; the active tab displays a website (GetTranscribe) and the browser tab bar with the new-tab (+) control is visible near the top of the window.

target.primary: Plus (+) new-tab button at the right end of the browser tab bar (top of the window).

post_action: A new browser tab is opened.
The browser shows the new tab / start page with an address/search bar visible.

steps.expected_current_state: Chrome window showing the Google homepage; the bookmarks bar is visible across the top and includes a bookmark for a Google Sheets file (spreadsheet bookmark is visible).
steps.intent: Open the Expenses Google Sheets file from the bookmarks bar.

target.primary: Bookmark in the bookmarks bar with a green Google Sheets icon labeled 'Expenses - Googl...' (near the top center of the window).

post_action: A new browser tab opens containing a Google Sheets document.
The spreadsheet titled 'Expenses' is displayed with the sheet and cells visible.

subtasks.text: Enter the next sequential index number in the new expense row, then populate the Description and Cost cells using the extracted receipt details from {extract_0}. Expected outcome: A new expense row is filled with the extracted description and amount and the entry is committed in the sheet.

steps.expected_current_state: Google Sheets is open on the 'Expenses' sheet. The header row is visible and row 2 contains 'Test Bill' in the Description column while the 'Idx' (first) column for that row is empty.
steps.intent: Fill the index cell for the expense row that contains 'Test Bill'.

target.primary: Empty cell in the 'Idx' column (left of the 'Description' value 'Test Bill', row 2) near the top-left of the sheet

post_action: An index value is added to the 'Idx' cell for that row.
The active selection moves down to the next row.

steps.expected_current_state: Google Sheets open to the Expenses sheet showing columns like 'Idx', 'Description', and 'Cost'. A cell in the 'Idx' column on the third row is ready to be edited (active cell near the left side of the sheet).
steps.intent: Enter an index number into the empty cell in the 'Idx' column for the new row.

target.primary: Cell in the column labeled 'Idx' on the third row (the empty cell directly below the row containing '1'), near the left side of the sheet.

post_action: The previously empty cell in the 'Idx' column becomes populated with text.
The active selection moves to the Description cell to the right.

steps.expected_current_state: Google Sheets document titled 'Expenses' is open in a browser. The sheet grid and toolbar are visible; row 2 contains an existing entry ('Test Bill') in the Description column and row 3 is visible and empty. No modal dialogs are open.
steps.intent: Select the Description cell for the next expense row so the user can enter a description.

target.primary: Cell in the 'Description' column on the row labeled '2' (the second data row) — the empty cell directly under the 'Description' header

post_action: The Description cell for that row becomes selected and enters edit mode.
A text cursor appears and characters are visible in the cell.

steps.expected_current_state: Expenses Google Sheet open in a browser. The Description cell for row 3 (B3) is in edit mode with a partial entry visible and a blue edit outline; sheet toolbar and headers are visible.
steps.intent: Enter the full expense description into the Description cell for row 3.

target.primary: Cell in the 'Description' column, row 3 (B3) — the cell with a blue edit outline near the top-left of the sheet.

post_action: The Description cell displays the newly entered text.
Focus moved to the Cost cell in the same row (the adjacent cell in the 'Cost' column).

steps.expected_current_state: Google Sheets 'Expenses' spreadsheet open in a browser showing columns including 'Description', 'Cost', and 'Invoice Number (if available)'. The row containing 'small cappuccino at black point cafe' is visible and its Cost cell is currently not active.
steps.intent: Select the Cost cell for the 'small cappuccino at black point cafe' row so an amount can be entered.

target.primary: Empty cell under the header 'Cost' in the same row as the description 'small cappuccino at black point cafe' (visible in the sheet)

post_action: The Cost cell in that row becomes the active/selected cell.
A blue outline and active cell handle appear indicating the cell is ready for input.

steps.expected_current_state: Google Sheets open in a browser showing the 'Expenses' spreadsheet. The sheet grid with headers like 'Description' and 'Cost' is visible and a cell in the Cost column for the second data row is active/selected for editing.
steps.intent: Type the cost $7.19 into the active Cost cell for the 'small cappuccino at black point cafe' entry.

target.primary: The Cost cell in the same row as the description 'small cappuccino at black point cafe' (the active/blue-selected cell in the Cost column).
target.fallback: Cell C3 under the 'Cost' header (third row of the sheet).

post_action: The Cost cell for that row now contains the newly entered text.
The cell remains selected with the sheet showing the updated entry.

steps.expected_current_state: Google Sheets open in a browser showing the 'Expenses' sheet; a cell in column C (row 3) is active and in edit/entry mode with a visible numeric value and blue selection outline.
steps.intent: Finish and commit the entered cost value for the active cell so editing ends.

target.primary: Active cell in the sheet grid showing a numeric value (blue outline) in column C, row 3 (cell with visible '$7.19')

post_action: The cell edit is committed and the cell exits edit mode.
Selection/focus moves away from the edited cell (typically to the next cell).
